Whiskey Library | Full time | Remote, worldwide

Whiskey Library is looking for a curious, commercially minded marketer with deep Google Ads expertise. You will develop the messaging, write the copy and run the experiments that grow our Bourbon Mystery Box subscription and online bottle shop.

You will have room to form a point of view, put it into practice and improve it through testing. Working directly with our CMO, creative team and landing-page designer, you will take ideas from customer insight through to execution and the next iteration.
About Whiskey Library

We help people discover great craft whiskey through our Bourbon Mystery Box, a monthly subscription of full-size bottles chosen around their tastes, and our online bottle shop.

We buy single barrels and small blends directly from craft distilleries and independent bottlers, with both names on the label. We also carry bottles from their core ranges. That gives you a mix of familiar producers and distinctive selections to market.

We are a small, global, fully remote team. We value ownership, speed and high-quality output over process or hierarchy.

• Assess acquisition cost, order value, gross profit and customer lifetime value, with clear separation between branded and non-branded activity, subscriptions and retail.

• Share findings with the wider marketing team, turn their insights into new tests, and follow through independently on agreed work.

You will make routine account decisions independently. Budget increases, offer changes and major shifts in strategy are agreed with our CMO, particularly when they affect other channels.

• Strong marketing judgment and writing ability. You can connect customer insight to persuasive copy and explain why a message fits the brand.

• Curiosity demonstrated through your work: questions you investigated, assumptions you challenged and ideas you changed when the evidence surprised you.

• Proven ecommerce Google Ads execution, with practical knowledge of Merchant Center, product feeds, conversion tracking, Google Analytics and attribution.

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

- Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant - Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry - Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

- Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world - Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

You will make Proxima's plasma simulation stack trustworthy by confronting it with reality. You will be the person in the group who lives at the intersection of modeling and experiment: fluent enough in the physics to know what a model should predict, and close enough to the diagnostics to know what the data can actually support.

- Reconstruct the plasma state from real diagnostic measurements using our time-dependent Bayesian state-estimation workflow (Thomson scattering, interferometry, CXRS, ECE, XICS, bolometry, magnetics), with calibrated uncertainties, and benchmark it against established analyses such as Minerva/IDA reconstructions and ASTRA power-balance res
